segments.text: What's up guys welcome back to Crime Time Snacks. On June 7, 2021, 52 year old Maggie Murdoff texted
a friend. She said her husband sounded fishy and was up to something. A few hours later she was dead.
To understand how this happened you have to look at the Murdoff family.
They were a massive legal dynasty in the South Carolina Low Country.
Alex's grandfather and father ran the local prosecutor's office for decades.
Alex Murdoff followed right in their footsteps. He graduated from the University of South Carolina's
School of Law in 1994. He worked as an attorney at the family's prominent private law firm and
volunteered at the prosecutor's office. Alex was married to Maggie who was known locally as a

They had two sons, Buster and 22 year old Paul. In the summer of 2021 the family was already

named Mallory Beach. She was a passenger on a boat Paul allegedly drove into a bridge while drunk

visit his father who was terminally ill. Maggie agreed but she was suspicious. That is when she

phone. He told dispatchers he had just discovered the bodies of his wife and son on the ground
and that they were not breathing. The case file shows both victims were shot multiple
times at close range. They were hit in the head, wrists and chest. Investigators quickly
noted that two different guns were used in the killings. We have to look closer at that 2019

The boat actually belonged to Alex Murdoch. There were six people on board that night.
The crash killed Mowry Beach and injured two other passengers. In April 2019, Paul was
officially charged with three felonies including boating under the influence causing death.
The case file shows Paul had a blood alcohol content of 28.6. That is more than three times the
legal limit for an adult driver. To get the alcohol, Paul used an ID belonging to his older
brother Buster. What happened immediately after the crash caused massive local outrage.
Despite allegedly driving the boat, Paul was never handcuffed. He was not given a field

father, Randolph Murdoch III. Randolph had also served as the local prosecutor. Now, he was 81

meetup. She was reportedly considering ending her marriage to Alex. In fact, she had consulted

know is exactly what she expected to happen when she got there. She walked into a situation
that investigators would spend years trying to fully unpack. Alex's initial story to police was

That night, Maggie already knew something was off. We know she texted her friend about Alex

The Solicitor website notes he has been elected five times since, most recently in 2024.
The investigation into the murders eventually blew the lid off Alex's financial history.
By 2023, the record shows Alex faced a staggering 102 grand jury criminal charges.
He was hit with 19 indictments relating to fraud and drug offenses. 99 of those charges came from the

The murder case itself became a massive media event. News outlets called it

On May 13, 2026, the South Carolina Supreme Court made a massive ruling that unanimously

Prosecutors have already stated they plan to retry the case.
Alex initially claimed that at the time of the killings he had been with his mother, who has

He pleaded not guilty. On the witness stand, he later admitted repeatedly lying to law officers

The state Supreme Court ruled 5-0 in favor of Alex's appeal. They stated that the jury's

South Carolina Attorney General Allen Wilson quickly released a statement following the ruling.
He said his office respectfully disagreed with the decision but would aggressively seek to retry
